extra.message: User-controlled query parameter 'username' is directly interpolated into an SQL SELECT statement via f-string. An attacker can inject SQL by passing a value like '" OR 1=1 --' to extract all user records, including password hashes.

All fields from the User model (name, username, password, address, email, contact) are directly interpolated into an SQL INSERT statement via f-string without parameterized queries. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL through any of these fields.
User-controlled query parameter 'username' is directly interpolated into an SQL DELETE statement via f-string. An attacker can inject SQL to delete arbitrary records or modify the database.

User-controlled 'user.address' is directly interpolated into an SQL DELETE statement via f-string without even surrounding quotes. This makes exploitation trivial — an attacker can supply an address like '1; DROP TABLE users; --' to execute arbitrary SQL.

The raw JSON body from the request is passed directly as a MongoDB query object to get_nosql_users(). An attacker can send MongoDB query operators such as {"$gt": ""} or {"$ne": ""} or {"$regex": ".*"} to extract all user records, bypassing any intended query filters.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: The POST /reset endpoint resets the entire database (SQL and NoSQL) without any authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated user can wipe all data, causing complete denial of service.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The DELETE /user endpoint allows deletion of any user by username or address without any authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated client can delete arbitrary users from the database.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The PUT /user endpoint allows creation of users without any authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated client can insert arbitrary user records into the database.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: When run_sql_query returns multiple rows, it returns raw tuples via {'users': _data} which include the password hash column (index 3). The single-row path explicitly maps fields and omits the password, but the multi-row path exposes all columns including password hashes to callers such as the /select endpoint.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log or Debug File

extra.message: MD5 is used to hash passwords (md5(user.password.encode()).hexdigest()). MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsuitable for password hashing — it is fast to brute-force and vulnerable to collision attacks. Should use bcrypt, scrypt, or argon2.
